nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Tropical sunshine drives algae growth in the clear shallows and on the rocks of the lake edge.

nodes.name: Lake water and nutrients
nodes.desc: A huge, deep, clear freshwater lake. Its nutrients and plankton carry the open-water food chains.

nodes.name: Seasonal rains
nodes.desc: Rain feeds the lake and wets the lakeshore woodland, helping trees such as baobab and fig grow.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae, plants and animals, returning nutrients to the water and soil.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny floating algae that form the base of the open-water food chain in the lake.

nodes.name: Rock algae (aufwuchs)
nodes.desc: A film of algae and small organisms growing on rocks, grazed by rock-dwelling cichlids.

nodes.name: Baobab
nodes.desc: A huge, long-lived tree of the dry woodland around the lake. It is recorded often near the park.

nodes.name: Rock fig
nodes.desc: A fig that grows on rocky outcrops near the shore. Its fruit is recorded in the diet of birds such as the bulbul.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Small drifting animals such as copepods, cladocerans and ostracods that graze phytoplankton.

nodes.name: Chambo
nodes.desc: Tilapia that feed mainly on phytoplankton. They are an important food fish for people and wildlife.

nodes.name: Mbuna
nodes.desc: Colourful, mostly endemic rock-dwelling cichlids, often specialised feeders on algae growing on rocks.

nodes.name: Yellow baboon
nodes.desc: An opportunistic omnivore of the park that eats fruit and seeds, including baobab.

nodes.name: Common bulbul
nodes.desc: A common, widespread songbird that eats fruit such as figs.

nodes.name: Lake fly (kungu)
nodes.desc: Its larvae eat zooplankton and are food for fish. Adult swarms feed birds and are harvested by people.

nodes.name: Utaka
nodes.desc: Open-water cichlids that feed in schools on zooplankton.

nodes.name: Predatory haps
nodes.desc: Large cichlids that prey on other fish. Livingstoni plays dead to lure prey close.

nodes.name: Pied kingfisher
nodes.desc: Hovers over open water, then plunges to catch fish. It also takes crustaceans and large aquatic insects.

nodes.name: Hamerkop
nodes.desc: A wading bird of shallow water that mainly eats amphibians and fish, and a generalist hunter.

nodes.name: Nile monitor
nodes.desc: A generalist predator and scavenger eating fish, eggs, carrion, frogs, insects, birds and small mammals.

nodes.name: African fish eagle
nodes.desc: Fish are its main prey, snatched from a perch with its talons. It is the most-recorded bird of the area.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: An ambush predator that mostly eats fish, but also takes land animals at the water edge, and scavenges.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A secretive big cat of the park. Baboons are a regular prey for leopards across southern Africa.
